title: Collections
name: The collections desk
tagline: Know who to call. Know what is actually owed.
summary: A practical desk for prioritising overdue accounts, checking returns and credits, and keeping follow-ups accountable.
problem: An open invoice does not always mean a collection call is the right next step. Unposted returns, unapplied payments and active disputes can make the balance misleading.
approach: Separate collectible balances from exceptions first. Then prioritise the remaining accounts by age, exposure and contact history, with one owner and a specific next action.
decision: Put return and reconciliation issues with the team that can clear them. Give collectors a focused list of genuinely payable invoices.
sop: Confirm delivery and inspect any open return request before asking for payment.
Check for a credit memo, replacement, unapplied cash or an active dispute.
Explain invoice terms politely without arguing about the statement date.
Record the outcome, next contact date and promise details.
Escalate unresolved exceptions with evidence and a named owner.

title: Chargebacks
name: Dispute resolution studio
tagline: Build the case before the deadline builds pressure.
summary: A case register that connects deadlines, evidence, refund hand-offs and the next step in a dispute.
problem: Disputes arrive with incomplete context. Some need a defensible response; others reveal a refund or hand-off the business should have completed already.
approach: Keep case research, support requests and submitted rebuttals as separate stages. Match each dispute theme to an evidence checklist and investigate the underlying customer journey.
decision: Prioritise the next deadline, establish whether the refund is genuinely owed, and prepare a concise evidence bundle for review.
sop: Log both case identifiers, report date, stated deadline and filed reason.
Investigate the order, delivery, return, credit and refund history.
Ask for processor guidance without marking the rebuttal as submitted.
Collect the evidence appropriate to the actual facts of the case.
Record submission separately and retain the response confirmation.

title: Team training
name: The team learning room
tagline: Turn experience into a process someone else can run.
summary: A structured learning path with practical case decisions, a 30-day ramp, coaching records and a knowledge assessment.
problem: A new colleague can make calls before they understand what makes an invoice collectible. Activity rises, but incorrect asks and avoidable escalations rise with it.
approach: Teach the decision before the script. Move from account checks to supervised customer conversations, then to independent work with a clear quality standard.
decision: Release a learner to independent work after practical demonstrations and documented coaching, rather than after an arbitrary number of calls.
sop: Week 1: understand delivery status, aging, returns, credits and account history.
Week 2: shadow calls, practise polite terms explanations and log dispositions.
Week 3: handle supervised follow-ups and prepare evidence-based escalations.
Week 4: demonstrate independent decisions and consistent documentation.
Use observed examples and specific feedback for the next coaching session.

title: Audits
name: Quality & controls lab
tagline: Inspect the work that protects the customer.
summary: A risk-focused quality review with weighted call criteria, evidence gaps, exception ownership and coaching actions.
problem: A high call count can hide poor account checks, unclear commitments and weak documentation. A broad average can also hide one serious control failure.
approach: Review account preparation, communication, payment accuracy, follow-up ownership and documentation separately. Keep critical failures visible alongside the score.
decision: Use the score to guide coaching, and treat a critical privacy or payment-handling failure as a separate escalation.
sop: Select a mix of random calls, escalations and high-value interactions.
Review the account evidence before listening to the conversation.
Score observable behaviour against the published criteria.
Record critical failures separately from the average quality score.
Assign a specific coaching action, due date and follow-up review.

title: Client handling
name: Client relationship desk
tagline: Own the relationship across every hand-off.
summary: A multi-location client view linking unresolved issues, commercial opportunities, review cadence and recovery plans.
problem: A client with many branches experiences one supplier, while internal teams see separate invoices, calls and return requests. Nobody sees the full relationship.
approach: Bring branch issues into one account plan. Coordinate with the central contact, separate service recovery from expansion discussions and agree a visible follow-up rhythm.
decision: Resolve the service obstacle, confirm ownership with the client, and pursue growth only when the relationship is ready for it.
sop: Map the central contact, branch stakeholders and the client's payment process.
Consolidate branch queries into one clear reconciliation or service summary.
Agree the next step and keep the client informed until it is resolved.
Identify expansion needs through useful discovery questions.
Track opportunities separately from booked revenue and confirmed commitments.

title: Customer database
name: Customer data workbench
tagline: Make the customer record reliable enough to act on.
summary: A data stewardship workbench for inconsistent names, missing contacts, possible duplicates and ownership of corrections.
problem: Inconsistent identifiers and contact records waste calling time, break account matching and send work to the wrong person.
approach: Preserve raw records, standardise an explicit set of fields, flag uncertain matches and keep corrections traceable to an owner.
decision: Approve a correction with evidence. Flag a possible duplicate for review instead of merging two customer accounts automatically.
evidence: Downloadable SQLite database and SQL queries
sop: Preserve identifiers as text, including leading zeroes.
Validate required fields and distinguish blanks from genuine zero values.
Normalise names and contact formats while retaining the original value.
Review possible duplicates using more than a similar name.
Log the approved correction, evidence, owner and date.

title: Cash flow
name: Cash planning room
tagline: See the cash consequence of the next decision.
summary: A 13-week cash plan with clear opening cash, receipts, payments and adjustable timing assumptions.
problem: An open balance is not cash available to spend. Payment timing, refunds and operating commitments affect the cash position week by week.
approach: Build a visible cash rollforward and keep receipts, supplier payments, payroll and refunds distinct. Make the assumptions easy to challenge.
decision: Compare a timing downside with the base plan before committing cash, and assign follow-ups to the receipts that matter most.
sop: Set the opening cash balance and the date of the forecast.
Separate expected receipts from already received cash.
List payroll, suppliers, refunds and other commitments explicitly.
Stress receipt timing and refund outflows without changing the base inputs.
Review forecast against actual receipts and explain significant variances.

title: Performance reviews
name: The performance review desk
tagline: Make the review useful for the next week of work.
summary: A balanced team view of activity, contact, promises, follow-up compliance and quality, with specific coaching commitments.
problem: Ranking colleagues by cash alone can reward easy accounts and overlook quality, follow-up discipline or a difficult portfolio.
approach: Compare activity, contact outcomes and quality together. Discuss the account mix before choosing one observable improvement for the next review.
decision: Agree a specific action, the support needed and the date to review the evidence. Keep the review focused on work that the colleague can influence.
sop: Prepare the period, account mix and source definitions before the meeting.
Compare contact and follow-up outcomes alongside activity and quality.
Ask the colleague to explain obstacles and bring examples.
Agree one measurable behaviour and the support needed.
Record a review date and assess the next period against that commitment.

FROM "reviews"
GROUP BY "agent"
ORDER BY records DESC;

title: Meetings
name: The decision room
tagline: Leave the meeting with a decision, an owner and a date.
summary: A meeting workspace that turns operational issues into a focused agenda, clear decisions and a follow-through register.
problem: Meetings repeat the same unresolved issues because a discussion was recorded without a clear decision, owner or due date.
approach: Bring a short pre-read, link each agenda item to evidence and close the discussion with a recorded next step.
decision: Use meeting time for the decision that needs the group. Track execution outside the meeting with a named owner and deadline.
sop: Send a brief pre-read with the issue, evidence and decision required.
Invite the people who can make the decision or own the action.
Separate informational updates from items needing discussion.
Record the decision, owner, due date and any dependency.
Begin the next meeting by closing or escalating overdue actions.
